source: CIC-IDS-2018, 7 capture days (Wed14/Thu15/Fri16/Fri23/Wed28/Thu01/Fri02) downloaded from the CIC AWS bucket; 6.16M windows, window 30, all 5 classes

transition_only.finding: On all-window F1 persistence wins (0.947 vs 0.836) - the autocorrelation artifact. On the 31,781 windows where the stage changes, persistence scores 0.000 and the model 0.391 (BSS +0.52). Infiltration transition F1 (0.562) exceeds its all-window F1 (0.415).

calibration.finding: ECE 0.0045 before scaling - already well calibrated (CrossEntropy is a proper scoring rule and classes are learnable). T~1.03.

world_model_rollout.verdict: PASS: beats both persistence and the window mean -- the state head learned genuine dynamics
world_model_rollout.finding: PASS - beats persistence (+0.226) AND the window mean (+0.068), holds skill for all 10 rollout steps. Genuine learned dynamics, unlike the CTU-13 checkpoint which lost to the window mean.

fusion_weight_ablation.note: multiclass macro_f1 is label-space-mismatched on DAPT (7-stage chain preds vs 5-stage DAPT labels); binary attack/benign SEDI is the meaningful axis
fusion_weight_ablation.finding: Cross-dataset binary SEDI rises monotonically with model weight: pure rules (0.0) -0.256, pure model (1.0) +0.050. The hand-written port rules help in-dataset but hurt generalization to unseen networks. Argues to raise MODEL_WEIGHT above the current 0.30 for deployment.

cross_dataset_dapt.finding: Cross-dataset attack recall 29.5% - markedly worse than the classification-optimized base_w30 (79.7%). This checkpoint was selected on onset AUC, which optimizes transition forecasting at the cost of raw breach-head transfer. The onset head itself DOES transfer: k5 AUC 0.639 vs persistence 0.500. Honest tradeoff: onset-optimized forecasting vs classification-optimized detection are different objectives.
